title: Manchester United appoint Manchester City’s academy head of coaching Darren Hughes
content:
Manchester United have appointed Darren Hughes in a new role as the club’s head of academy football development and methodology.

Hughes joins United from Manchester City, where he held multiple roles across the past 12 years and was most recently the club’s academy head of coaching.

In the new post, Hughes will report to United’s academy lead Stephen Torpey, who joined the club last year after a stint as Brentford’s academy director. Torpey replaced Nick Cox — who had overseen United’s youth system for six years before joining Everton — in the role.

Both Hughes and Torpey are part of the reshaping of United’s academy following Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s investment in early 2024, with director of football Jason Wilcox providing oversight.

Wilcox previously worked with Hughes and Torpey at City, where the latter was also head of coaching and played a role in player recruitment. That period saw City’s youth graduates Rico Lewis, Cole Palmer and James McAtee all advance into the first-team squad.

In October, Ratcliffe criticised United’s academy and said he wants youth production at Carrington to help improve finances at the club.

The United co-owner had said the academy “had really slipped”, despite the club fielding a youth-team graduate in every first-team matchday squad since 1937.

Earlier this month, United hired Ian Broomfield as a casual scout covering the under-21 market. Broomfield’s arrival followed Connor Hunter, who has been at United since 2013, being promoted to head of academy recruitment.
